headline_marked: [[Jeddah mission thought executed Bangladeshis faced prison]] not death penalty, Foreign Ministry tells MPs
headline: Jeddah mission thought executed Bangladeshis faced prison not death penalty, Foreign Ministry tells MPs
summary: Officials at Bangladesh's Jeddah mission believed two executed Bangladeshis were serving prison terms, not facing the death penalty, due to unclear Saudi lists. Dhaka was not notified prior to the October 14 executions.
details: Bangladesh's mission in Jeddah mistakenly believed two Bangladeshi nationals executed in Saudi Arabia were facing prison terms, not the death penalty. This revelation was made by the foreign ministry to a parliamentary committee yesterday.

The two Bangladeshis were executed on October 14 without prior notification to Dhaka. They had been detained since August 2023 on separate allegations, one for “cybercrime” and the other for “adultery”.

The foreign ministry informed the committee that Saudi Arabia had sent a list of approximately 2,500 prisoners about 14 days before the executions. However, the cases of the two Bangladeshis were not properly identified on this list, with the sentence column left blank.

The Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has sought answers from Saudi authorities regarding this oversight. They also requested a report on potential negligence at the Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah and measures to prevent similar incidents.

A foreign ministry official, speaking anonymously, explained that while Saudi Arabia can impose the death penalty for cybercrimes against the kingdom and for adultery, such sentences are extremely rare for these specific offenses. Previous records often showed prison sentences for adultery.

The parliamentary committee also addressed reports of abuse faced by Bangladeshi women workers in Saudi Arabia and other Middle Eastern countries. The ministry reported that around one to two percent of the 169,000 Bangladeshi women workers in Saudi Arabia face abuse, with 1,364 women domestic workers rescued and repatriated.

headline_marked: [[DGFI members among 6 arrested]] over alleged kidnapping of businessman in Dhaka
headline: DGFI members among 6 arrested over alleged kidnapping of businessman in Dhaka
summary: Six people, including two DGFI members, were arrested in Dhaka for allegedly kidnapping a businessman and demanding Tk 100,000 ransom. The victim managed to escape and alert police.
details: Six individuals, including two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) and one from the Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party, have been arrested in Dhaka. They are accused of allegedly kidnapping a businessman and demanding a Tk 100,000 ransom.

The victim, Md Sharif, a motorcycle dealer from Shyamoli, was reportedly lured to a house in Chandrima Model Town on Saturday under the pretext of buying a motorcycle. Once there, he was allegedly assaulted and held captive while the ransom was demanded.

Sharif managed to pay Tk 70,000 but was beaten again because the group was unhappy with the amount. Around 3 AM, he was moved to a vehicle near Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, where he spotted a police patrol and sought help, leading to the arrests.

Police intervened, confirmed the kidnapping, and detained the six suspects. The arrests became complicated when two suspects were identified as DGFI members, requiring verification from Army Headquarters before formal arrest and court appearance.

The arrestees include DGFI Sergeant Al Mamun, 39, and Lance Corporal Nuruzzaman, 31; Ansar member Sohel Rana, 32; private company security guard Mukul Gazi, 26; Mahfuzur Rahman, 22; and Ziaul Islam, 35. Two others, Sonia, 30, and Fonirul (also known as Monirul), 45, have also been accused in the case.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ashraful Haque subsequently sent all six arrested individuals to jail. The case was filed by Md Sharif at Mohammadpur Police Station.
